Yippee Noodle Manchurian

The beloved Indo-Chinese classic gets a Yippee! makeover — crispy noodle-stuffed balls tossed in a tangy, spicy Manchurian sauce. An irresistible main course that is pure comfort food!

20 mins
25 mins
3
Medium

Ingredients

For the Noodle Balls

  • 2 packs Sunfeast Yippee! Magic Masala noodles (with tastemaker)
  • 1 cup cabbage, finely shredded
  • ½ cup carrot, grated
  • 3 tablespoons cornflour
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Oil for deep frying

For the Manchurian Sauce

  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 inch ginger, grated
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon chilli sauce
  • 1 tablespoon tomato ketchup
  • 1 teaspoon vinegar
  • 1 teaspoon cornflour dissolved in ¼ cup water
  • Spring onions to garnish
  • 1 tablespoon oil

Method

  1. Cook Yippee! noodles as per pack instructions. Drain, cool, and chop roughly.
  2. Mix the noodles with shredded cabbage, grated carrot, Yippee! tastemakers, cornflour, all-purpose flour, salt, and pepper. Shape into small balls.
  3. Deep fry the noodle balls on medium heat until golden and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper.
  4. For the sauce: heat oil in a pan. Add garlic and ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds.
  5. Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, and vinegar. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
  6. Add the cornflour slurry and cook until the sauce thickens.
  7. Toss the fried noodle balls in the Manchurian sauce. Garnish with spring onions.
  8. Serve hot immediately.

Serving Suggestion

Serve Yippee Noodle Manchurian hot as a main course alongside plain steamed rice or fried rice. Add a bowl of hot and sour soup on the side for the full Indo-Chinese restaurant experience at home!

Chef's Tips

  • Squeeze out all moisture from the cabbage before mixing — this keeps the noodle balls firm and crispy.
  • Fry the noodle balls in small batches to maintain oil temperature and ensure even crisping.
  • Toss the balls in the sauce just before serving to keep them crispy.
  • For a dry version (without gravy), skip the cornflour slurry and just coat with the sauce.
